title: Multipartite dynamics beyond bipartite entanglement equilibration
authors: Yan Liu, Ya-Wen Sun, Ren-Jie Ying, Jun-Yuan Zeng
abstract: Entanglement equilibration need not mark the end of quantum-information dynamics in quantum thermalization. We show that the complete Schmidt spectra of a fixed tripartition can become stationary while its multipartite correlation structure, distinguished by local-unitary invariants, continues to evolve. This separation occurs exactly within a finite window in self-dual kicked-Ising dynamics and asymptotically in Haar-random circuits. We further demonstrate an independently tunable timescale for multipartite dynamics using quantum-error-correcting codes. When coupled to a locally scrambling bath, ordinary entanglement approaches equilibrium through rapid local scrambling, while weak logical--bath coupling drives a slower reorganization of multipartite correlations. These results reveal a deeper distinction than the ordering of equilibration times: bipartite entanglement and multipartite correlation structure can probe distinct physical channels of quantum-information dynamics, rather than merely different stages of the same relaxation process.
summary: This work establishes a fundamental distinction between the equilibration of bipartite entanglement and the evolution of higher-order multipartite correlations. By analyzing systems like kicked-Ising chains and error-correcting codes, the authors show that these two aspects of quantum information dynamics can proceed on entirely different timescales. This suggests that entanglement measures are insufficient to characterize the full complexity of quantum thermalization.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether multipartite correlation structure can continue to evolve and probe distinct physical dynamics even after bipartite entanglement measures appear to have reached equilibrium.
main_result: Bipartite entanglement and multipartite correlation structure can evolve independently, demonstrated by observing that multipartite invariants continue to change while reduced density matrices plateau in specific models.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and numerical simulations on engineered quantum systems, employing specialized multi-entropy invariants and analyzing time evolution across different coupling regimes.
model_or_system: The study analyzes several models: the self-dual kicked-Ising (SDKI) chain, Haar-random circuits, and a quantum error-correcting code coupled to a locally scrambling bath.
key_observables: Complete Schmidt spectra, local-unitary (LU) invariants (e.g., $G$), and various entropy measures ($S_n, G$).
important_parameters: Coupling strengths ($\lambda$), system size ($N$), and time evolution windows ($t$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on specific model constructions (SDKI, QEC) and uses approximations like the conditional-frame approximation for certain calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the plateauing of bipartite states (SDKI) while multipartite invariants vary, and show the evolution of correlations in the code-bath system.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from general observations of entanglement equilibration to specific, controlled demonstrations using SDKI dynamics, and finally to advanced analysis of protected logical dynamics in QEC codes coupled to baths.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical framework for distinguishing between different physical mechanisms governing quantum thermalization, which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems dynamics.
